steps.content: A few days have passed since the last interrogation.
Ring—Ring—
You stare at the comms interface, which has barely gone off for the past few days, and give a bitter smile.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief...
Probably another request to release Chelsea on bail. Who's it this time? Some governor or commander?
Chelsea has shown you the power of money indeed. These few days, the Bureau's internal comms system has been overwhelmed with thousands and thousands of messages to you.

For the past few days, the office phone's been ringing nonstop, and the mailbox is overflowing. Contents include everything from "let's discuss the price" to "watch out for your life." They're all asking for one thing: to release Countess Chelsea.
Its scale and number of people are beyond your expectations. You can't imagine how many people are involved in this money web.
At first you plan to ignore them. But you received a note from an FAC special agent yesterday during a mission, on which the words "Release Her" were written with blood.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: They're using more and more aggressive means.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm curious to see what they will do for money.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It's not my place to interfere with your decision, but the Bureau will be further restricted if this goes on.
Instead of wasting time with this endless stream of people, why not just go to her cell and deal with the root of trouble?
The thought of Chelsea's room gives you a headache. Apart from the locked door, the place has nothing to do with the MBCC now.

At your insistence, Chelsea is still locked up in her room. But the room has been re-painted and renovated, with velvet wallpaper, expensive carpets, and lots of antique furniture decorated with gems. It's like a copy of her room in the Countess' Court.

You've been trying to stop it, but those officials and nobles kept pressuring the Bureau through various connections. There's even a group of Sinners outside Chelsea's room, waiting to see you make a fool of yourself.
Nightingale also suggested that you don't need to bother with such trivial matter like renovations.
So you decided not to even go near it. Out of sight, out of mind. But now, you have to face this luxurious room again, with the greatest factor of uncertainty in it—Countess Chelsea.
Before you even get close to her room, you see a mountain of gifts casually piled up by the door. All the gifts are for Countess Chelsea, and there are too many to fit in the room.
Chelsea faces against the door with her whole body sinking into the fluffy, luxury sofa. She holds a comms in one hand as if she's listening to some message.
You're about to open the door when the message coming from the comms brings you to a halt.

steps.speaker: Unknown male voice
steps.content: Your Excellency, what's a mere Chief to you? All you need is to give an order. I can make him fall from here any minute! If you wish, I also have the ultimate means to shut...
steps.female_content: Your Excellency, what's a mere Chief to you? All you need is to give an order. I can make her fall from here any minute! If you wish, I also have the ultimate means to shut...

steps.content: Before the message finishes playing, there is a crunching noise as the comms is crushed to pieces. Its sharp parts cut Chelsea's hand. The blood, affected by her powers, turns into tiny gems, spilling onto the ground along with the broken pieces.
You can't see the expression on her face, but she is clearly very upset. Is it because of the message? Isn't that what she wants?

options: Open the door and go in

choices.text: Open the door and go in

steps.content: The noise prompts Chelsea to turn around swiftly. A gem solidifies in her hand, seeming like it's about to bash at the door.
At hearing your voice, the light in her hand fades in an instant.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Ahem... It's you, Chief. I was just working out.
To ease the awkwardness, she swings her right arm and kicks the comms pieces under the sofa.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: What brought you here? Have you decided to be my sugar baby?
I'm more concerned about what's under the sofa. I've received many similar greetings to that message recently.
You simply ignore her question about sugar baby and stare at her in all seriousness.
How are they related to you? Did you tell them to do this?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Chief... Are you suspicious of me? You're such a paranoid.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I have nothing to do with them. As I said, I'm not leaving until you agree to be my sugar baby.
Chelsea locks eyes with you, sitting on the sofa.

options: So what's with that phone call just now?

choices.text: So what's with that phone call just now?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: They're just bootlicking me for my money and gems, but trust me, I didn't accept any of them!

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I rejected them outright. I won't let them treat the person I like that way!
Chelsea leans closer to examine your facial expression.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Come on... Why do you still look so sad, Chief?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: That's not good! Here, have a drink and leave all your troubles behind!
She takes a bottle from the table on the side, removes the cork, and pours the red liquid into a glass, chuckling as she hands you the glass.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Want some? It's N.F.82 Collection drink! I bought it with three gems a couple of days ago. It's superb. Just one sip will make you forget all your troubles!
You look happy.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Yes—I've got so much money, enough to get all the fun I can have, and I get to see my favorite person every day. If this isn't happiness, what is?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: If I ever feel down and unhappy, I spend money—there's always something you can buy that makes you happy—that's what everyone says.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Well... I'm referring to my master and... people who hang out with me. It was like that, and it still is.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I grew up learning jewelry craftsmanship from my master. At first, there was nothing in my life other than my master and the gemstones. People would always smile when I gave them gems, no matter what happened to them.
Some happiness can't be bought with money.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Like what? That hasn't really happened to me. Care to give me an example, Chief?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Not really. I had the chef from the best luxury hotel in Eastside cook for me for a whole day and night. And I had the most famous singer in Eastside sing for me for a whole day.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I asked them if they were tired. They said not at all, and told me to let them know anytime I want their company again.
How much did you pay them?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Hmm? Not much, I guess. I just filled their pockets with gems.
Chelsea seems to think that this kind of contracted relationship equals company, like what she typically does. Looks like you need to convince her from a different perspective.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: But do not lose your way... Come. Come to Maria City. Here, you shall find the path to <color=#fb9259>vanquishing evil</color>...
Chelsea makes a big stretch and runs to poke her head through the door to peek at other Sinners.

options: Money can't buy sincerity from the heart

choices.text: Money can't buy sincerity from the heart

steps.content: Those who experienced sincerity from the heart, they smile when they look back on their memories. And that's something you can't buy with money.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: ...You seem to have a point.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: But those moments, I can record them! How about that? I'm smart, aren't I?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Speaking of which... My master once hired a famous director in Eastside to film a documentary! One that recorded my growth as a lapidarist! I was the protagonist!
Chelsea gets up from the sofa and finds a disc-like object after rummaging around on the bookshelf.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Oh! This is it! Chief, is there a projector here? Let's get one and watch it together! I remember being very happy back then. I wonder if watching it will make you happy too!
There is one, but...

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: But what? It's too much trouble?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Not a problem at all. Here, take this gem. Give it to your staff, whoever gets the projector here.
Chelsea is instinctively trying to solve problems with money again.
No, it's not about money. The projector hasn't been used for a while and I'm not sure if it still works.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Oh... I see. Then I'll just give this gem to you, Chief! Let's go get the projector here!
You and Chelsea move the projector into her room. Chelsea inserts the disc into the machine, and the big screen begins to flicker.

steps.speaker: Guest
steps.content: How can I wear this kind of brooch? It looks ridiculous.

steps.speaker: Gemsmith
steps.content: Th-This is the most classic style and craftsmanship...

steps.speaker: Guest
steps.content: Humph. This design is already outdated. And look at this cut mark. It's ruined such a good gem! What a waste. I don't think I'll come back to this shop... Oh? Let me take a look at that brooch.

steps.speaker: Guest
steps.content: Hmm... Fashionable and perfectly-crafted. Your craftsmanship can't be that bad if you could turn such a poor-quality gem into this. Make me another one like this with the best gem.

steps.speaker: Gemsmith
steps.content: Oh, Chelsea! Your craftsmanship is getting so much better! A merchant offered a huge amount of money just to have you cut gems for them!

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Is that so... Sure. Coming right up.

steps.speaker: Gemsmith
steps.content: But anyway, a family came to our shop with a cat, which I thought looked very pretty, so I bought it. Why don't you give it a name?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Aww it's so cute! Let's call it... Sitri.
Looks like your documentary is pretty inspiring.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Haha... You flatter me, Chief. I'm almost a bit embarassed.
The scene in the documentary changes abruptly. Chelsea, who seems to realize something, suddenly goes up and turns off the video.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Because the rest of it... isn't important.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: After that, my master found me some friends, who took me to the dinner parties only the upper class in Eastside could go. I only had to carve a few gems to get all kinds of exotic treasures and compliments from those friends.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: At an auction, I bought a gem. But before I could get my hands on it, I was told that the old Count had taken it and left double the price as compensation.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: The old Count was indeed richer. My master and I could never acquire such an extortionate amount of wealth accumulated over several generations in our lifetime.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: And later, under my master's recommendation, I was invited by the old Count to work under him, carving gems just for him.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: For me, it was just making gems in a different place and with a more stable amount of orders.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: But... it also meant that I didn't get to see my master very often. Every time he came to see me was to get me to take him to experience the so-called luxurious life. He didn't even craft gems so much anymore.
He just liked your money.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Perhaps. But I don't think there's anything wrong with that. Everyone I know tells me that you can be happy as long as you have money.
And you think so too?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Yup... It can buy everything, so it's the best thing in the world!

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: We visited so many places, like the best casinos in Eastside and the best cruises...

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I've never seen anything like it before. Those friends I had never took me to luxurious entertainment venues like that.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: We made a lot of friends. Every day was a different experience. It was all very exciting.
Has he had enough of it and ready for a life of leisure?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: He died.
He died? How?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: He was already quite old, and he spent all his time in places like that, having lavish meals.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: It's only natural that he died of illness. I understand my master all too well. It's impossible for him to leave this kind of life.
Weren't you sad?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: ...To be honest, I didn't feel anything when my master died, and I don't know why. I just thought it was a pity.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I heard that he was still muttering about his jewels to his last breath.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: After he died, I took over all the Count's jewel crafting. He paid me more money and sent me checks with larger and larger amounts.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: But I knew that he had more money than that. When one has enough money, one can get whatever they want, that is, power.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: The old Count's wealth and power are all mine now. What happiness can't I buy?

options: Are you and your sugar babies truly happy?

choices.text: Are you and your sugar babies truly happy?

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: To be honest, I don't know.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: But I guess... Sitri must be very happy.
Humans and cats are probably different.
She avoids your eyes by averting her gaze toward the ceiling, then laughs after a few seconds.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Why don't you try being my sugar baby, Chief? You never know until you try. Then you'll be able to tell me the answer!
The typical bright grin, frivolous words, and heartless looks make the Chelsea who plunged into the memory just now seem like a short-lived blossom.
No, thanks. I'll be happy if those people leave me alone.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Don't worry, Chief! I'll stop them all! If anyone doesn't listen... Hmm, I'm going to show them what they'll get when they upset someone I like.

options: Is this your sweet nothings again?
I'm not going to be tempted.

choices.text: Is this your sweet nothings again?
I'm not going to be tempted.

steps.content: At hearing this, Chelsea shows a swooning face and reaches out to place her hand on your shoulder. You quickly dodge her hands, to which she shrugs in response.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Chief, you just sweep me off my feet. My affection for you grows more and more each day.
I hope you remember what you promised. I gotta go now. Goodbye.
You turn around and leave. Even after a good distance out of Chelsea's room, you can still hear her enthusiastic goodbyes.

Hopefully, she will keep her word and deal with those troubles. You suddenly realize that you haven't checked your mailbox and wonder how many new threatening letters you got today. You should probably have a look.
You come to the mailbox. Just when you're about to open it, a shadow sneaks out behind you, then you pass out after a series of electrical noises...
Alone in the room with the lights off, Chelsea turns on the video recorder again.
In the video are her, Sitri, and her master.

steps.speaker: Gemsmith
steps.content: What? You accidentally burned the snow fox fur? It's okay. Just buy a new one. It's not that expensive. Make sure you finish the Count's order today!

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Okay.
After the master leaves, Chelsea sinks into the pile of gems in the room, as if she's zapped of all her energy.
Sitri carefully reaches out its paw and gently touches Chelsea's forehead. When it finds that Chelsea doesn't mind, it rolls its entire body toward her.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Haha... It tickles!

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Sitri, are you happy being with me?

steps.speaker: Sitri
steps.content: Meow—
Sitri throws itself into her arms as if it's answering her question.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: Yeah...? That's great.

steps.speaker: Chelsea
steps.content: I'm so glad you're happy.
